technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Kafka for Kafka integration, leveraging existing Spring Framework capabilities.
Implement global configuration defaults using application properties with per-deployment overrides via environment variables or YAML profiles.
For Sqoop features, utilize the existing Sqoop API and CLI commands, wrapping them with a Spring service layer.
Adopt a modular approach separating Kafka and Sqoop features into distinct modules within the same codebase.
Use JUnit 5 and Spring Test for unit and integration testing, with Testcontainers for Kafka and embedded Sqoop where possible.
Implement acknowledgment (ACK) through Spring Kafka's manual acknowledgment mode and custom listener containers.
For request-reply (bindRequestor/bindReplier), use Spring Kafka's request-reply pattern with reply topics and correlation IDs.
Batching will be implemented using Spring Kafka's batch listener and producer batching settings (batch.size, linger.ms).
Sqoop job stop will be implemented by calling Sqoop's job termination API or executing a CLI command with process management.
Sqoop log access will be achieved by redirecting Sqoop's output streams to a logging framework (e.g., Logback) and streaming via standard logging mechanisms.
Incremental data load will use Sqoop's --incremental flag with last-value tracking stored in a database or file.
assumptions: The existing codebase already includes Spring Boot, Spring Kafka, and Sqoop dependencies.
The developer has a working local environment with Kafka and a sample Sqoop setup.
All user stories are independent and will be implemented in a single development cycle.
Effort estimates include design, coding, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each story.
Acceptance tests (U1) will be run in CI but assumed CI pipeline can be extended without major overhead.
Documentation includes inline code comments, JavaDoc, and a brief user guide for new features.
Code reviews are performed by the same developer (self-review) and refinement time is included.
No additional training or research time is needed beyond typical familiarity with Spring and Kafka/Sqoop.
All estimates are in work-hours for a single experienced developer.

activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, clarify ambiguities, and finalize acceptance criteria for each feature.

activities.activity_name: Design and Architecture for Kafka Features (U1-U5)
activities.activity_description: Design the configuration structure, concurrency and compression support, ACK mechanism, request-reply pattern, and batching within the Kafka integration module.

activities.activity_name: Design and Architecture for Sqoop Features (U6-U8)
activities.activity_description: Design the stop-job functionality, log capturing and streaming mechanism, and incremental data load tracking for Sqoop integration.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U1 – Acceptance Test Coverage for Kafka
activities.activity_description: Write automated acceptance tests using Spring Kafka test support, set up test containers for Kafka, and integrate with CI pipeline.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U2 – Concurrency and Compression Support for Kafka
activities.activity_description: Add global and per-deployment configuration for consumer concurrency and producer/consumer compression types. Implement property overrides and corresponding Spring Kafka configuration.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U3 – ACK Messages for Kafka
activities.activity_description: Implement manual acknowledgment mode option for Kafka consumers, including configuration and listener container customization.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U4 – bindRequestor and bindReplier for Kafka
activities.activity_description: Implement bindRequestor (producer expecting async replies) and bindReplier (consumer handling requests and sending replies) using Spring Kafka's request-reply pattern with correlation IDs and reply topics.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U5 – Batching Support for Kafka
activities.activity_description: Add batching configuration options (batch size, linger time) for Kafka producers and batch listener support for consumers.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U6 – Stop Sqoop Job
activities.activity_description: Implement functionality to stop a running Sqoop job via API or CLI command management, including error handling and state tracking.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U7 – Access Sqoop Logs
activities.activity_description: Capture Sqoop output logs and stream them to the application's logging mechanism (e.g., Logback). Implement log retrieval and streaming.

activities.activity_name: Implementation of U8 – Incremental Data Load for Sqoop
activities.activity_description: Implement incremental data load using Sqoop's --incremental flag, store last imported value, and retrieve only newer rows.
Perform end-to-end integration tests combining Kafka and Sqoop features, ensuring no regressions and proper interaction between modules.
Write user documentation covering new configuration options, usage examples, and update JavaDoc for new classes and methods.
Self-review code for quality, consistency, and best practices; refactor where necessary.
Update CI configuration to run acceptance tests (Kafka), add new build steps if needed, and prepare deployment artifacts.
